basic_information.name: Self-RAG / Corrective RAG (CRAG)
basic_information.creator: Self-RAG: University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI (Ai2), IBM Research (Akari Asai, Zeqiu Wu, Yizhong Wang, Avirup Sil, Hannaneh Hajishirzi). CRAG: University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) (Shi-Qi Yan, Jia-Chen Gu, Yun Zhu, Zhen-Hua Ling).
basic_information.description: Self-RAG and Corrective RAG (CRAG) are two complementary advanced RAG patterns that introduce self-reflection and self-correction mechanisms into the retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. Self-RAG trains a single LM to adaptively decide when to retrieve, then generates and critiques its own outputs using special reflection tokens (Retrieve, ISREL, ISSUP, ISUSE), enabling on-demand retrieval and multi-faceted quality assessment. CRAG adds a lightweight retrieval evaluator (fine-tuned T5-large, 0.77B parameters) that scores retrieved documents and triggers corrective actions: refine if correct, discard and web-search if incorrect, or combine both if ambiguous. Together they represent the state-of-the-art in self-corrective RAG, reducing hallucinations and improving factual accuracy by ensuring the model only uses relevant, high-quality retrieved context. Both patterns are now widely implemented in LangGraph, LlamaIndex, and other orchestration frameworks as foundational building blocks for agentic RAG systems.
basic_information.release_date: Self-RAG: October 2023 (arXiv), published at ICLR 2024 (Oral, top 1%). CRAG: January 2024 (arXiv), revised October 2024.
basic_information.license: Self-RAG: MIT License (GitHub repo). CRAG: MIT License (GitHub repo). Both are open-source research implementations.
basic_information.github_stars: Self-RAG (AkariAsai/self-rag): ~2,200 stars (as of early 2026). CRAG (HuskyInSalt/CRAG): ~437 stars, 46 forks (as of early 2026).

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Self-RAG: End-to-end fine-tuned LM architecture with expanded vocabulary including four reflection token types. Uses a three-model training pipeline (Retriever, Critic, Generator) but at inference only the Generator LM is needed (single model). Critic model is used offline during training data creation. CRAG: Plug-and-play middleware architecture with a lightweight retrieval evaluator (T5-large fine-tuned), a decompose-then-recompose knowledge refinement module, and web search fallback. CRAG sits between retriever and generator as a corrective layer, compatible with any RAG pipeline.
technical_architecture.language: Self-RAG: Python (PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM for inference). CRAG: Python (PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers).
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Not directly applicable as both are RAG patterns/frameworks, not embedding models. They work with any embedding model and vector store. Self-RAG uses Contriever-MS MARCO as its default retriever.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: Not directly applicable. Both patterns are retriever-agnostic and work with any indexing algorithm (HNSW, IVF, flat, etc.). Self-RAG uses Contriever with FAISS for passage retrieval in its reference implementation.
technical_architecture.scalability: Self-RAG: Inference requires a single fine-tuned LM (7B or 13B parameters), uses segment-level beam search with reflection token scoring. Can skip retrieval entirely for simple queries, reducing latency. Scales with standard LLM serving infrastructure (vLLM). CRAG: Lightweight evaluator (0.77B T5-large) adds minimal overhead. Web search fallback introduces external dependency but improves robustness. Plug-and-play design means it scales with the underlying RAG system.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Both patterns can be deployed anywhere an LLM can run: cloud-managed (AWS, GCP, Azure), self-hosted (Docker, Kubernetes), or on-premises. Self-RAG models available on Hugging Face Hub (selfrag/selfrag_llama2_7b, selfrag/selfrag_llama2_13b). CRAG's evaluator is a fine-tuned T5-large, deployable on modest GPU hardware. LangGraph and LlamaIndex provide ready-to-use implementation templates for both patterns.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Self-RAG: Adaptive on-demand retrieval. The model generates a [Retrieve] token to decide whether to retrieve (yes/no/continue) at each generation segment. Can retrieve multiple times, skip retrieval entirely, or retrieve mid-generation. Uses dense vector retrieval (Contriever-MS MARCO by default) but is retriever-agnostic. CRAG: Standard dense retrieval as first pass, then evaluates quality and conditionally augments with web search (e.g., via Tavily, Google Search API). Supports any initial retriever. Three-tiered action system: Correct (refine existing), Incorrect (discard + web search), Ambiguous (combine both).
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Both patterns are chunking-agnostic and work with any chunking strategy. CRAG additionally applies a decompose-then-recompose algorithm that strips retrieved documents into fine-grained 'knowledge strips' (sentence-level units), scores each for relevance, and recomposes only the relevant strips. This is effectively a post-retrieval chunking refinement step.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Self-RAG: Uses reflection tokens as an implicit reranking mechanism. The ISREL token scores document relevance (Relevant/Irrelevant), the ISSUP token evaluates whether generated text is supported (Fully Supported/Partially Supported/No Support), and segment-level beam search with weighted critique token probabilities effectively reranks generation candidates. CRAG: The T5-large retrieval evaluator provides explicit document-level scoring (-1 to 1 confidence), functioning as a lightweight reranker with threshold-based routing.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Neither Self-RAG nor CRAG natively support multimodal retrieval in their original implementations. Both are text-focused patterns. However, the architectural principles (adaptive retrieval, quality evaluation, corrective actions) can be adapted to multimodal settings, and recent agentic RAG frameworks building on these ideas support multimodal contexts.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: Not natively supported in either original implementation. Both focus on passage-level retrieval from flat document stores. However, the self-reflection and corrective mechanisms are orthogonal to the retrieval source and can be combined with Graph RAG approaches. CRAG's plug-and-play design makes it particularly amenable to graph-enhanced retrieval pipelines.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Self-RAG: Strong built-in citation and grounding capabilities. The ISSUP (Is Supported) reflection token explicitly evaluates whether each generated segment is grounded in retrieved evidence. Self-RAG shows significant gains in citation accuracy for long-form generation, outperforming ChatGPT on citation precision and recall metrics. CRAG: Indirect grounding through the knowledge refinement step, which ensures only relevant knowledge strips are passed to the generator. No explicit citation token mechanism, but the filtering step reduces hallucination risk.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Self-RAG: Addresses context window limits through selective retrieval (only retrieves when needed) and segment-level generation with per-segment retrieval decisions. Does not stuff all retrieved passages into context at once. CRAG: The decompose-then-recompose algorithm effectively compresses retrieved documents by filtering irrelevant knowledge strips before passing to the generator, reducing context window usage. Web search results are also refined before injection.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Self-RAG: Inference latency depends on the number of retrieval calls triggered. For queries where retrieval is skipped, latency matches standard LM inference. For queries requiring multiple retrievals, segment-level beam search adds overhead proportional to beam width and number of retrieval steps. Using vLLM for inference helps. Overall, RAG systems typically add 40-50% latency overhead to TTFT compared to vanilla LLM inference. CRAG: The T5-large evaluator adds a lightweight forward pass (~0.77B parameters) per query. Web search fallback adds network latency (typically 1-3 seconds per web search call). For 'Correct' paths (no web search needed), overhead is minimal.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Self-RAG: Throughput depends on the underlying LLM serving infrastructure (vLLM recommended). The adaptive retrieval mechanism can improve throughput for simple queries by skipping unnecessary retrieval. Segment-level beam search may reduce throughput for complex queries. CRAG: Throughput is primarily determined by the base RAG pipeline. The evaluator adds a small constant overhead. Web search fallback can become a bottleneck if triggered frequently.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: Self-RAG 13B benchmark results: PopQA accuracy 55.8% (vs. Llama2-13B 14.7%, Alpaca-13B 24.4%), TriviaQA accuracy 69.3% (vs. Alpaca-13B 66.9%), PubHealth accuracy 74.5% (vs. Alpaca-13B 51.1%). Self-RAG 7B: PopQA 54.9% (vs. Ret-ChatGPT 51.8%). CRAG improvements over baseline RAG (using SelfRAG-LLaMA2-7B): +7.0% on PopQA, +14.9% FactScore on Biography, +36.6% on PubHealth, +15.4% on Arc-Challenge. CRAG improvements over baseline RAG (using LLaMA2-hf-7B): +2.1% on PopQA, +2.8% FactScore on Biography.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: Self-RAG: Evaluated on six diverse tasks including open-domain QA (PopQA, TriviaQA), fact verification (PubHealth), reasoning (Arc-Challenge), and long-form generation (Biography with FactScore, ASQA). Self-RAG significantly outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat across all tasks. Published at ICLR 2024 as an Oral paper (top 1%). CRAG: Evaluated on four datasets (PopQA, PubHealth, Biography, Arc-Challenge) covering short-form and long-form generation. CRAG is plug-and-play and demonstrates consistent improvements when applied on top of different base models and RAG approaches.

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Excellent ecosystem integration. LangGraph: Official tutorials for both Self-RAG (langgraph_self_rag) and CRAG (langgraph_crag, langgraph_crag_local). LlamaIndex: Official Corrective RAG workflow implementation (CorrectiveRAGPack). DSPy: Self-RAG principles align with DSPy's programmatic approach to LM optimization; DSPy modules can implement Self-RAG-style self-reflection. Haystack: Custom pipeline components can implement both patterns. Both patterns are commonly combined with Adaptive RAG in LangGraph's official tutorial (langgraph_adaptive_rag), which unifies query analysis with active/self-corrective RAG.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Self-RAG: Original implementation fine-tunes LLaMA-2 (7B, 13B). Models available on Hugging Face (selfrag/selfrag_llama2_7b, selfrag/selfrag_llama2_13b). The LangGraph implementation pattern is model-agnostic and works with any LLM (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, open-source). CRAG: Retrieval evaluator is fine-tuned T5-large. The pattern itself is model-agnostic for the generator. LangGraph implementations commonly use OpenAI GPT-4, Anthropic Claude, or local models via Ollama.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: No native MCP server for Self-RAG or CRAG as standalone tools. However, LangGraph (the primary implementation platform) has MCP integration capabilities, and agentic RAG systems built with LangGraph can expose Self-RAG/CRAG workflows as MCP-compatible tools. The pattern-level integration is indirect through orchestration frameworks.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Both patterns are data-source-agnostic at the architectural level. Self-RAG: Original uses Wikipedia passages indexed with Contriever + FAISS. In practice, works with any vector store (Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, etc.). CRAG: Supports any initial retrieval source plus web search augmentation (commonly via Tavily AI, Google Search API, or Bing). The web search fallback is a key differentiator, allowing CRAG to access real-time information beyond static knowledge bases.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: No built-in observability. Both patterns can be instrumented through their orchestration framework: LangGraph integrates with LangSmith for tracing and monitoring, LlamaIndex integrates with Arize Phoenix and Langfuse. Self-RAG's reflection tokens provide natural observability signals (retrieval decisions, relevance scores, support scores, utility scores) that can be logged and analyzed. CRAG's evaluator confidence scores and action routing (Correct/Incorrect/Ambiguous) provide similar observability hooks.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Both are open-source research patterns with MIT licenses, free to use. Costs are driven by the underlying infrastructure: LLM inference costs (per-token for hosted APIs or GPU compute for self-hosted), retrieval costs (vector database queries), and web search API costs (CRAG). Self-RAG requires a fine-tuned model, so there is a one-time training cost if fine-tuning your own model, or you can use the pre-trained models from Hugging Face.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Both patterns are completely free to implement. Pre-trained Self-RAG models are freely available on Hugging Face Hub. CRAG's T5-large evaluator can be trained on accessible hardware. LangGraph and LlamaIndex implementations are open-source. The only costs are infrastructure (compute, API calls, web search).
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Self-RAG: Primary cost is LLM inference. A 7B model requires ~14GB VRAM (FP16) or ~7GB (INT8). Cloud GPU costs: ~$0.50-1.00/hour on AWS (g5.xlarge). Self-RAG's adaptive retrieval can reduce costs by skipping unnecessary retrieval calls. Estimated cost: $0.002-0.01 per query depending on retrieval frequency. CRAG: Adds the T5-large evaluator inference (~$0.0001-0.001 per query). Web search API costs when triggered: Tavily ~$0.01 per search. For high-traffic applications, web search fallback costs can accumulate; optimize by tuning confidence thresholds.
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: For a production Self-RAG/CRAG system: (1) GPU compute for LLM inference: $500-2000/month for moderate traffic (1000-10000 queries/day). (2) Vector database: $50-500/month depending on scale. (3) Web search API (CRAG): $100-1000/month depending on fallback frequency. (4) Fine-tuning cost (one-time for Self-RAG): $100-500 on cloud GPUs. (5) Engineering time for implementation: 2-4 weeks with LangGraph templates. Using hosted LLM APIs instead of self-hosted models shifts costs to per-token pricing but eliminates GPU management overhead.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Both patterns are foundational to the self-corrective/agentic RAG paradigm that became dominant in 2025-2026. Self-RAG is a seminal paper (ICLR 2024 Oral, top 1%) with high academic impact and practical influence. CRAG is a widely-adopted pattern for production RAG systems due to its plug-and-play nature. Together, they represent the most referenced approaches for advanced RAG quality control. By 2026, agentic RAG (heavily influenced by these patterns) is considered the baseline for production AI applications. The RAG market is projected to grow from $1.96B (2025) to $40.34B by 2035 at 35% CAGR.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Self-RAG and CRAG are research patterns rather than commercial products, so they don't have traditional 'customers.' However, their principles are adopted in: (1) Healthcare AI systems (CRAG patterns for hallucination elimination, achieving 0% error in iodinated contrast media consultation). (2) Legal document analysis (corrective RAG for high-accuracy requirements). (3) Enterprise knowledge systems incorporating self-corrective retrieval. (4) IBM Research (co-author affiliation for Self-RAG). (5) LangChain/LangGraph ecosystem (official tutorials and recommended patterns). (6) Educational and research institutions using Self-RAG for factual content generation.
adoption_and_market.community_size: Self-RAG GitHub: ~2,200 stars. CRAG GitHub: ~437 stars, 46 forks. Both papers are highly cited in the RAG research community. Self-RAG paper has significant citations on Semantic Scholar and Google Scholar. LangGraph's CRAG and Self-RAG tutorials are among the most-visited pages in their documentation. The broader agentic RAG community (encompassing these patterns) spans LangChain Discord (100k+ members), LlamaIndex Discord, and active discussions on Reddit, Hacker News, and X/Twitter.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Not applicable as standalone patterns. Self-RAG: Academic research funded by University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI (Ai2), and IBM Research. Akari Asai recognized as MIT Technology Review Innovator Under 35 (2025) for this work, now joining Carnegie Mellon University as professor. CRAG: Academic research from USTC's National Engineering Research Center of Speech and Language Information Processing.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main alternatives and related approaches: (1) Adaptive RAG: Combines query classification with Self-RAG/CRAG for routing simple vs complex queries. (2) Speculative RAG: Uses draft-then-verify approach with smaller specialist models. (3) RankRAG: Unifies context ranking with RAG in a single LLM. (4) FLARE (Forward-Looking Active Retrieval): Iterative retrieval based on generation confidence. (5) Standard RAG with reranking: Simpler but less robust to irrelevant retrievals. (6) Agentic RAG with tool use: More flexible but higher latency. Self-RAG's key differentiator is end-to-end training with reflection tokens. CRAG's key differentiator is its plug-and-play nature and web search fallback.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Self-RAG and CRAG are highly relevant for startups building AI-powered knowledge systems, especially in high-stakes domains (healthcare, legal, finance) where hallucination reduction is critical. Recommended use cases: (1) Startups with 2-10 engineers can implement CRAG as a quick upgrade to existing RAG pipelines using LangGraph templates (1-2 weeks). (2) Teams with ML expertise can fine-tune Self-RAG models for domain-specific applications. (3) CRAG's web search fallback is ideal for startups in news, market intelligence, or real-time data domains. (4) Budget-conscious startups should start with CRAG (no fine-tuning needed) and graduate to Self-RAG as data and requirements grow. (5) For regulated industries (EU AI Act compliance), the self-correction and grounding mechanisms help meet explainability and accuracy requirements.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Build (recommended for most startups): Both patterns are well-documented with official LangGraph tutorials. CRAG can be implemented in 1-2 days using LangGraph's official template with any LLM API (no fine-tuning needed). Self-RAG can use pre-trained Hugging Face models or be implemented as a LangGraph workflow with any LLM. Buy: Enterprise RAG platforms (Vectara, Glean, Cohere RAG) incorporate similar self-corrective mechanisms. Consider buying if: (1) you need production-ready SLAs immediately, (2) your team lacks ML engineering capacity, (3) you need enterprise features (SSO, audit logs, compliance). Self-host Self-RAG models if you need data privacy or have predictable high-volume workloads.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: CRAG with LangGraph: 1-2 weeks for a basic production implementation. Self-RAG with pre-trained models: 2-4 weeks including evaluation and tuning. Self-RAG with custom fine-tuning: 4-8 weeks including data preparation, training, and evaluation. Combined Adaptive RAG (Self-RAG + CRAG): 3-6 weeks for a well-orchestrated production system. Key accelerators: LangGraph official templates, pre-trained Self-RAG models on Hugging Face, Tavily API for web search integration.
key_lessons: Start with CRAG before Self-RAG: CRAG is plug-and-play and requires no model fine-tuning. Implement it as a quality gate on your existing RAG pipeline first. Measure the improvement in hallucination rates before investing in Self-RAG fine-tuning.

Tune confidence thresholds per domain: CRAG's effectiveness depends heavily on the retrieval evaluator's confidence thresholds. The original paper uses different thresholds per dataset (e.g., 0.59/-0.99 for PopQA, 0.95/-0.91 for Biography). Invest time in calibrating these for your specific domain and document corpus.

Web search fallback is a double-edged sword: CRAG's web search improves coverage for real-time or rare queries but introduces latency, cost, and potential quality issues (web content may be unreliable). Monitor fallback frequency and consider caching strategies.

Self-RAG's reflection tokens provide built-in observability: Log the Retrieve, ISREL, ISSUP, and ISUSE token values to understand your system's behavior. High rates of 'No Retrieval' may indicate your knowledge base needs expansion; frequent 'Irrelevant' scores signal retrieval quality issues.

Combine with Adaptive RAG for production efficiency: Route simple factoid queries directly to the LLM (no retrieval), moderate queries through standard RAG, and complex or sensitive queries through Self-RAG/CRAG. This layered approach optimizes cost while maintaining quality where it matters most.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: No native no-code interface for either pattern. However, CRAG can be implemented through visual workflow builders: Dify and Flowise support conditional routing and document grading nodes. LangGraph Studio provides a visual interface for building and debugging Self-RAG/CRAG workflows. R2R (by SciPhi) offers a managed RAG platform with corrective retrieval features. For non-technical teams, the concepts are accessible through platforms like Vectara (Grounded Generation) or Cohere RAG, which embed similar quality-control mechanisms.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt Engineering & No-Code Tools): CRAG as an example of self-corrective AI patterns, web search augmentation. Session 3 (Framing & Managing AI Projects): Architecture decisions for RAG quality control, build vs buy analysis. Session 4 (AI Business Models & Strategy): Cost-performance tradeoffs of different RAG patterns, when self-correction adds business value.

confidence.data_quality: High. Both papers are peer-reviewed: Self-RAG at ICLR 2024 (Oral, top 1%), CRAG reviewed at ICML 2024. Official implementations available on GitHub with reproducible results. Strong academic citations. LangGraph official documentation provides verified implementations.
confidence.cross_reference: Self-RAG findings confirmed by: ICLR 2024 proceedings, IBM Research, Semantic Scholar citations (500+), LangChain blog, Hugging Face model cards, MIT Technology Review (Innovators Under 35). CRAG findings confirmed by: OpenReview, Semantic Scholar, DataCamp tutorials, LangGraph official documentation, multiple independent blog reproductions (Meilisearch, Analytics Vidhya, LearnPrompting). Benchmark results cross-referenced between arxiv papers and GitHub README implementations.
confidence.caveats: Self-RAG: (1) Requires fine-tuned models (original is based on LLaMA-2, now older); applying to newer models (LLaMA-3, Mistral) requires re-training. (2) Segment-level beam search adds inference complexity. (3) Self-reflection can occasionally lead to 'overthinking' where the model second-guesses correct outputs. (4) GPT-4 was used to create training data for the critic, creating a dependency on proprietary models during training. CRAG: (1) Effectiveness depends on the retrieval evaluator's calibration; poor calibration leads to cascading errors. (2) Web search fallback may return unreliable or biased content. (3) The T5-large evaluator was trained on specific datasets; domain transfer may require retraining. (4) Web search adds external API dependency and privacy concerns. Both patterns: The field is rapidly evolving; newer approaches (Speculative RAG, RankRAG, FLARE) may supersede specific mechanisms while building on the same principles.
confidence.security_posture: Known attack surfaces: (1) Knowledge base poisoning: Both patterns are vulnerable to PoisonedRAG-style attacks where adversarial documents are injected into the retrieval corpus. Self-RAG's reflection tokens provide some defense by evaluating relevance and support, but sophisticated adversarial examples can bypass these checks. (2) CRAG's web search fallback introduces additional attack surface through web content manipulation (SEO poisoning, adversarial web pages). (3) Self-RAG's GPT-4-generated training data could embed biases from the teacher model. (4) Neither pattern has built-in compliance features (SOC 2, HIPAA, etc.) in their reference implementations. Mitigations: Self-RAG's ISSUP token helps detect unsupported claims. CRAG's evaluator can be monitored for adversarial confidence patterns. Both benefit from standard RAG security practices (input sanitization, retrieval result filtering, output guardrails). For EU AI Act compliance, the self-reflection mechanisms provide a form of built-in explainability that can support audit requirements.
